prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: one 4:3 landscape painting for The Burnt Book Sanskrit learning story. Request 1536 x 1152 native output or the closest supported native 4:3 resolution. Refined Indian watercolor with restrained gouache on warm ivory paper; organic detail, quiet ochre, sage, dusty terracotta, muted indigo. Warm, gentle, evocative storytelling, consistent character design.
Canonical scene brief: The inner room of the village school library at morning: the Ācārya unlocking a carved door; high on a shelf a small grey spirit made of knotted cords and pebbles pointing at rows of books and muttering; Dādī and Śuka looking up at it; sunbeams full of dust.
Character appearances:
you: Always seen from behind or at a distance, face never detailed, so every learner can be the hero: a young person in a simple ochre kurta with a cloth shoulder bag.
dadi: A warm, sharp-eyed grandmother in her seventies, silver hair in a low bun, round spectacles, a cream cotton sari with a thin maroon border and a grey shawl; carries a cloth-bound notebook.
shuka: A bright green rose-ringed parrot with a red beak and a faint pink and black neck ring, a little scruffy, very expressive eyes; usually on your shoulder or Dādī's.
acarya: A very old, serene scholar with a white beard and a saffron shawl, a palm-leaf manuscript always under his arm, kind half-closed eyes.
ganaka: A small grey spirit made of knotted cords, with two round pebbles for eyes and a cord of beads trailing behind.
Phone-first composition: clear compact narrative grouping, essential faces, hands and objects comfortably inside all edges. Show the complete scene without border. No collage or multi-panel layout.
Writing is permitted by the owner. This particular scene needs no readable inscription; focus on its narrative. Do not invent scripts or fill small objects with pseudo-lettering. No watermark or UI.

image.brief: The inner room of the village school library at morning: the Ācārya unlocking a carved door; high on a shelf a small grey spirit made of knotted cords and pebbles pointing at rows of books and muttering; Dādī and Śuka looking up at it; sunbeams full of dust.

alt.en: A knotted-cord spirit on a high library shelf points at rows of books while Dādī and a parrot look up
alt.hi: ऊँची अलमारी पर गाँठदार डोरियों का भूत पुस्तकों की ओर इशारा करता, दादी और तोता ऊपर देखते

narration.en: Next morning the Ācārya unlocks the inner room of the library. High on a shelf, a knot of cords and pebbles is counting books, losing count and starting again. “That book, those books, that leaf,” it mutters, pointing at everything and naming nothing. Dādī says softly: “He needs a word for ‘that’ in every case.”
narration.hi: अगली सुबह आचार्य पुस्तकालय का भीतरी कक्ष खोलते हैं। ऊँची अलमारी पर डोरियों और कंकड़ों की एक गाँठ पुस्तकें गिन रही है, गिनती भूल रही है, फिर शुरू कर रही है। “वह पुस्तक, वे पुस्तकें, वह पत्र,” वह बुदबुदाता है, हर चीज़ की ओर इशारा करता और किसी का नाम न लेता। दादी धीमे से कहती हैं: “उसे ‘वह’ के लिए हर विभक्ति में शब्द चाहिए।”

gloss.en: That, those, of that, for that.

body.en: Only the first-case forms {{सः}} and {{सा}} show an {{स्}}; everything else starts with {{त्}}. Pronouns also borrow odd endings: for a masculine or neuter, {{तस्मै}} (for), {{तस्मात्}} (from) and {{तस्मिन्}} (in); for a feminine, {{तस्यै}}, {{तस्याः}} and {{तस्याम्}}. The plural genitive is {{तेषाम्}} and {{तासाम्}}.
body.hi: केवल प्रथमा के रूप {{सः}} और {{सा}} में {{स्}} दिखता है; बाक़ी सब {{त्}} से शुरू होते हैं। सर्वनाम कुछ विचित्र प्रत्यय भी लेते हैं: पुंलिंग और नपुंसक में {{तस्मै}} (के लिए), {{तस्मात्}} (से) और {{तस्मिन्}} (में); स्त्रीलिंग में {{तस्यै}}, {{तस्याः}} और {{तस्याम्}}। षष्ठी बहुवचन {{तेषाम्}} और {{तासाम्}} है।

meaning.en: a word that stands for a noun
meaning.hi: संज्ञा की जगह आने वाला शब्द

note.en: The coloured forms are the odd ones: {{तस्मै}}, {{तस्मात्}}, {{तस्मिन्}}, {{तेषाम्}}. The neuter is the same except {{तत्}}, {{ते}}, {{तानि}} in the first and second cases.
note.hi: रंगीन रूप विचित्र हैं: {{तस्मै}}, {{तस्मात्}}, {{तस्मिन्}}, {{तेषाम्}}। नपुंसक वैसा ही है, केवल प्रथमा और द्वितीया में {{तत्}}, {{ते}}, {{तानि}}।

note.en: Four singular forms end in {{स्याः}} or {{स्यै}} or {{स्याम्}}; the others are like {{लता}}.
note.hi: एकवचन के चार रूप {{स्याः}}, {{स्यै}} या {{स्याम्}} पर समाप्त होते हैं; बाक़ी {{लता}} जैसे हैं।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of that table.
prompt.hi: उस तालिका के छूटे रूप भरिए।

explain.en: Every form is in the masculine table above.
explain.hi: हर रूप ऊपर की पुंलिंग तालिका में है।

prompt.en: Fill in the missing forms of the feminine.
Join each form to its meaning.
prompt.hi: हर रूप को उसके अर्थ से जोड़िए।

prompt.en: Tap every form of “that” in the feminine.

success.en: “तासाम्,” you say, and the knot of cords loosens a little. It points at the shelf of poetry and at last names it: “तासाम् कवितानाम्…” Dādī nods. “Now he can count what is not in front of him.”
success.hi: “तासाम्,” आप कहते हैं, और डोरियों की गाँठ कुछ ढीली पड़ती है। वह कविता की अलमारी की ओर इशारा करता है और अन्ततः उसका नाम लेता है। दादी सिर हिलाती हैं। “अब वह उसे भी गिन सकता है जो सामने नहीं।”

failure.en: The cords stay knotted. “Of those”, feminine plural: {{तासाम्}}.
failure.hi: डोरियाँ गठी रहती हैं। ‘उनका’, स्त्रीलिंग बहुवचन: {{तासाम्}}।

body.en: Sūtra 7.2.102, {{त्यदादीनामः}}, makes the stem {{तद्}} end in {{अ}}; 7.2.106, {{तदोः सः सावनन्त्ययोः}}, turns its {{त्}} into {{स्}} before the first-case ending, giving {{सः}}. Then 7.1.14, {{सर्वनाम्नः स्मै}}, gives {{तस्मै}}; 7.1.15, {{ङसिङ्योः स्मात्स्मिनौ}}, gives {{तस्मात्}} and {{तस्मिन्}}; 7.1.17, {{जसः शी}}, gives {{ते}}; and 7.1.52, {{आमि सर्वनाम्नः सुट्}}, gives {{तेषाम्}}.

text.en: The odd masculine and neuter endings.
text.hi: पुंलिंग और नपुंसक के विचित्र प्रत्यय।
